headline: Secured $700M Nation Shield contract with Kuwait to deploy a nationwide AI-driven counter-drone network; expects to double annual revenue in FY27 and FY28 with no additional capital required
reasoning: EOS signed its largest-ever contract, a $700 million deal with the Kuwaiti government to build a nationwide counter-drone defence network called Nation Shield using its proprietary AI-driven command-and-control system, Neither. The CEO expects 80% of the contract volume to be executed within the first 12-18 months, implying a very significant boost to revenues in FY27 and FY28, including the potential to double annual revenue year-over-year. The company does not need to raise additional capital to execute the contract, as the May capital raise (linked to the Mars acquisition and working capital) is sufficient even if the 20% bank guarantee is not reduced. The win elevates EOS from a component/equipment provider to an integrated solution provider competing against large European prime contractors. Further contracts are expected to grow the order book further. The UK Ministry of Defence provided proactive support in securing the contract, and BAE Systems has formally agreed to use EOS's command-and-control system for future counter-UAS systems.
quote: 80% of the contract volume will be executed and realized over the next 12 to 18 months. So you can expect a significant boost of our annual revenue in the year 27 and 28. Very significant boost up. So we add as us, we expect that we can double our annual revenue year over year with this contract, and we expect further contacts to come to boost further our order book and the revenue over the next few years to come. So it's a fantastic outlook. And I want to mention one additional point. Uh, we assume, as I was mentioning before, that the bank guarantee will either be significantly reduced or completely waived. And even if it would stay as it is, we would not need to raise any additional capital to serve this bank guarantee. We are well equipped with a with a capital raise, which we've done in my in May this year. So there is no more need for any additional capital to execute this contract.
episode_title: EOS opens a new growth front

headline: Two major growth fronts: European high-energy laser weapons (Dutch strategic partnership, potential serial contract, Netherlands production facility) and Middle East counter-UAS systems (all GCC member states in advanced negotiations, Kuwait contract as trigger)
reasoning: Electro Optic Systems sees Europe as a significant growth market driven by the Russian threat and rising European defence budgets, which are expected to open new facilities and production opportunities. The Dutch government has announced a strategic partnership with EOS on high-energy laser weapons, with a first serial contract anticipated soon and a laser production facility planned for the Netherlands. Similar discussions are underway with other European governments. In the Middle East, the Kuwait contract is described as a trigger for a significant number of future contracts across all GCC member states, all of which are currently in negotiations with EOS for counter-UAS systems. The company also notes that a UK-based company, Byor Systems, has entered an agreement to use EOS's command and control system for all future counter-UAS platforms, underscoring EOS's growing position in the UK market.
quote: We see two particular growth markets. One is the European market. Given the actual political situation with the Russian threat and with a budget increase all across Europe, so that will result into the opening of additional facilities of the US within Europe. We are in discussions with various governments to set up local production lines. Recently, the Dutch government has announced a strategic partnership with EOS on high energy laser weapons. This will result, hopefully soon in the first serial contract for a high energy laser weapon system. And obviously we will react to that with opening a laser production facility in the Netherlands. And we have similar discussions ongoing with other European governments. So Europe is the one area of significant growth. The other one is the Middle East. Because of the geopolitical situation in the Middle East and because of our long lasting relationship with most of the governments there. The Kuwait contract is the trigger point for a significant number of future contacts to come and to come very soon. We are in discussions and advanced negotiations with, I would say, all GCC member states that there's not a single country which is not in negotiation with us for counter US systems.
episode_title: EOS opens a new growth front

headline: Targeting multi-billion dollar revenue within 3–5 years, driven by anti-drone, laser weapons and space control systems; guided FY revenue of $360–$400m with significant further growth expected next year
reasoning: Andreas Schwer, CEO of Electro Optic Systems, stated the company expects revenue of $360–$400 million for the current year, with a very significant increase anticipated next year driven by a growing order book and conversion rate. He highlighted the company's strong innovation pipeline that can be commercialised without heavy R&D investment, and cited momentum in anti-drone systems, laser weapons, and space control/warfare as key growth drivers. He expects EOS to become a multi-billion dollar revenue company within three to five years and aspires to be the world-leading system provider outside the United States in space control. He also noted plans for expanded production facilities in Europe and the Middle East, and a return to the US Army market at scale. Schwer emphasized a consistent track record of under-promising and over-delivering since 2022.
quote: We expect for this year the revenue being within 360 to $400 million and you we, you will see that we are very optimistic to increase this further on next year very, very significantly because of the order book and the conversion rate... In five years from now, we will have a multi billion dollar of revenue. I'm quite convinced about that, a huge order book. We will have a more international operational footprint with active production facilities in Europe, more in the Middle East. By that point in time, I expect that our US operation will deliver in large scale to the US Army... I believe that we will be the world leading system provider not only for anti drone systems but also for laser weapons and the world leading company outside United States of America in what you call space control, space warfare, the ability to engage against space debris and satellites from ground with high energy laser weapons.
episode_title: From Saudi defence to EOS: Andreas Schwer’s plan to build a global giant

headline: Turnaround complete after cutting 30% of staff, replacing management, renegotiating unfavourable Middle East contracts and commercialising shelf-ready IP in laser weapons and anti-drone systems
reasoning: Andreas Schwer joined as CEO in 2022 when the company was in distress due to its founder-led R&D focus leaving commercialisation neglected, an unfavourable Middle East contract, and COVID headwinds. The turnaround involved letting go of about 30% of staff, replacing the entire management team, exiting money-losing business lines, and concentrating on highly profitable product lines. The company now has over 250 systems deployed in Ukraine and 60+ integrated systems in the Middle East, generating real-time operational feedback that accelerates software development. The acquisition of MARS added an AI-driven command-and-control software platform called Nita, enabling EOS to offer fully integrated turnkey anti-drone solutions rather than just effector weapons.
quote: The company was founder LED the founder. He is one of the best laser physicist worldwide and obviously the focus of the company was very much on R&D and during that time they have missed the limits to commercialise and to reach out to key markets to make money out of all that. They were very much concentrated on generating those kind of IPS and that was the the main reason why the company got in distress. Another one was COVID during that point in time, plus one contract in the Middle East, which was signed under unfavourable terms and conditions. So all that's together, they're creating the kind of perfect storm. So it was not a rocket science to get the company back on track. We needed to renegotiate those contracts and starts to commercialise the products which was sitting almost ready on the shelf.
episode_title: From Saudi defence to EOS: Andreas Schwer’s plan to build a global giant

headline: Drone warfare evolving rapidly in speed, autonomy and swarm capability, requiring continuous real-time adaptation of software and hardware from defence suppliers
reasoning: The anti-drone sector is evolving faster than traditional defence procurement cycles can accommodate, driven by active conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. Companies with large deployed fleets and agile organisations that can iterate quickly have a structural advantage over larger primes with slower internal processes. Swarm capability, autonomy, and speed are the key threat vectors shaping current R&D priorities.
quote: So I want to turn now and ask you, because drone warfare is an area that is rapidly evolving, how do you stay ahead of changes in drone speed, autonomy and swarm capability? And what gives you that competitive advantage against other companies, particularly bigger companies? So we are greatly benefiting from the fact that we have hundreds of installed and deployed systems in the two major conflict areas of the day.
episode_title: From Saudi defence to EOS: Andreas Schwer’s plan to build a global giant
